- ### OSI Layer 1 Reflection

Layer 1 of the OSI model is the physical layer. In my network, for this lab, copper straight through and serial dce was primarily used to physically connect each device together. Physical cabling, ports, and power are considered to be a part of the first layer, because to send bits through, it uses a physical median like cables.

(Screenshot 2 of IT Environment Switch MAC Address Table)

- ### OSI Layer 2 Reflection

In this layer of the OSI model, this is where the encapsulated data is being framed. The frame is sent in the local network, because it follows a MAC address routing table, compared to IP address. This is how the switches decide what is the best path to take. Where it forwards the frame to the corresponding port of the device Mac address.

- ### OSI Layer 3 Reflection

IP addressing, subnetting, and routing are all a part of the third layer in the OSI model. To get packets through the layers and network, it moves it from one router to the next, until it reaches the router that the requested segmented network is on. It does this by pinging to different routers, and deciding the fastest path to get to the goal destination. Subnetting gives the ability for bigger networks to be segmented into smaller manageable networks.

# Part 2 – Protocol Security & OSI Layers 4–7

- ### TCP vs UDP Security

TCP is more secure than UDP. This is because it uses a process of a three way handshake. The steps are SYN, SYN/ACK, then ACK. where each step can be tracked and logged. This ensures that a connection is established before sending the data. Comparing this process to UDPs, it doesn’t use a three way handshake. It’s connectionless, so it just sends the data without making sure that there’s a connection that’s established. 

- ### OSI Layer 4 Reflection

With TCP and UDP they each have different use cases, based on their pros and cons. TCP is reliable, stateful, and has a logging and tracking system for implications of firewalls, IDS, or IPS. While UDP, is faster and operates in a stateless behavior. This means that the security trade-off of using TCP and UDP is the speed at which data is being sent. 

- ### HTTP vs HTTPS Security

The difference between HTTP and HTTPS is the level of security, with HTTPS being more secure than HTTP. HTTPS is able to prevent Man in the middle attacks, because it encrypts data before it is sent over. Instead of data being in cleartext it’s encrypted, so the man in middle won’t be able to decipher the text. There’s also integrity checks, which detects if there’s a change in text before and after the data is transmitted. Then the server authenticates it with their certificate, proving that it’s correct. 

- ### OSI Layer Mapping for Encryption

HTTPS/TLS encryption happens in the seventh layer of the OSI model. It could also be consider in the sixth and fifth layer. This is because the data and instructions, known as the payload, are generated by applications running on source. Keeping the data from the previous layer (layer 4\) and TCP secure. 

- ### Why SSH Replaced Telnet

SSH is the more modern standard and has replaced Telnet. SSH has provided better security for networks. Telnet would send data or credentials in plaintext, so eavesdroppers would be able to see it, and decipher it very easily. However, SSH encrypts the message that you are trying to send, so eavesdropping wouldn’t occur. With the new standard of SSH it has impacted the overall improvement of security, because credential theft and session hacking are far more difficult to do now.

# Part 3

There was a process to the shellshock vulnerability attack. It exploited the vulnerability of using HTTP, in order to get access to remote code execution through a web server. Running arbitrary code in a remote environment. There was a flaw in a version of Bash that made web servers or shellshock in this case vulnerable. With the requested information, it was easily received or returned to the attack. Through the method of injection.   
Connecting the shellshock vulnerability to a LAMP Stack. There were multiple components that were involved in this attack chain. Linux, Apache, and Bash were used in the attack. Starting with Linux, following it was Apache, and then Bash.   
With remote code execution access the attacker was able to do multiple things. Overall they were able to gain information. With their attack lateral movement could continue further. This turns into gaining access or control to multiple end devices. These end devices controlled public health and safety for millions. This would be the Scada systems of the water and wastewater system.   
There are multiple ways that could have mitigated or prevented this attack. To start, they could have been up to date with their version of Linux, Apache, and Bash. This would mitigate the vulnerability that was exploited in Bash. Another way is to monitor their security system. Keeping logs and alarms to track when an attack is happening. This would decrease the chance of it being a dramatic negatively impacting attack. It would also mitigate lateral movement within their system and attack. Lastly, segmenting their network into different departments. Where if one department was infiltrated the others wouldn’t be. This connects to subnetting and lateral movement.   
Now, there’s different organizations like SEI CERT Coordination Center to help coordinate vulnerability disclosures and patch distribution. Organizations like these, if kept up to date and followed by their network, can help mitigate an attack. Knowing what it is that you could be possibly vulnerable to and new updates to keep up to date with multiple components. 

# Part 4

### Root Cause Analysis

| Vulnerability Category | What Went Wrong | Security Control That Was Missing |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| Unpatched Software | An outdated Bash Version was used, providing a vulnerability of attack.  | A patching system, whether that be one that automatically updates Bash and or  periodic update checks to see if a new update is available to use.  |
| Network Segmentation | Not having a segmented network, this caused ease of access to the entire network and it’s harder to mitigate the attack.  | Having a network infrastructure that has different segmentations for different environments. In this case it would be the OT environment. Other segmentation could be the IT environment, like shown in the lab. |
| Access Controls | The majority have insufficient access controls. Allowing users to have too much control in a system, then what is needed for their assignment. | Using the principle of least privilege to control access of users. |
| Monitoring & Detection |  Not including a monitoring, detection, or risk assessment system. When an attack does occur they wouldn’t know or know how to mitigate the attack. | Implementing a logging and monitoring system. Using secure ports and protocols can also help with the use of logging and monitoring. Where if there’s an attempted attack, the detection can alert you to it.  |

### Comprehensive Remediation Plan

In immediate containment which is the first twenty four hours, there’s actions that can stop ongoing damage. Locating the attack and how it was done. Which is capturing forensic evidence through logs. WBMUD could also isolate the affected segmented network, so that it wouldn’t spread or lateral move to other parts of the network.  
	Next, is the short-term fixes that can be implemented. The time frame of this is one day to one week. There’s multiple technical fixes that should be implemented immediately after this attack. The first is patching the system. Where you update the outdated software and all other outdated software. This would prevent future attacks and could help remedy the attack. Enabling logging is another way, if not already implemented. Monitoring how it’s affecting the network system. This provides information to help narrow down what was negatively affected and how to go from who or what was negatively impacted.  
Then comes the long-term improvements that would prevent similar incidents. The time frame of this would be from one month to three months. Using network segmentation to divide the network into smaller and more manageable networks. Managing these would be easier because you could isolate what happens in each segmented network. Another concept to implement is zero trust principles. Where you don’t trust anyone or anything, before allowing sending or receiving data. Then all users that are using this data are verified through valid credentials. Only those who are verified, which will be logged and monitored, have access, only until after they have verified themselves. This means that the system doesn’t trust them until after this process. There’s also implementing the principle of least privilege. Defining what users or groups have access to what. This would be access control across their network. There’s many things that should be implemented or changed in order to prevent future attacks and incidents that can occur.  
	There’s continuous monitoring capabilities that WBMUD should implement. Having a monitoring system would have detected the incident earlier. This would in turn reduce the cyber incident window of opportunity.   
Therefore, many organization processes and policies are in need of updating, in order to improve their cyber security. There needs to be people who are working on cyber security in the network like a CISO. Where there would be an emphasis on cyber security being an important part of the company. Overall, staff need to be trained and informed to spot an attack and keep data confidential. Instead of using unsecured paths, there could be an implementation of only using ones that are more secure like TCP.  

# Conclusion

	Through this lab, I learned many aspects of segmented critical infrastructure networks. Networks follow the foundational ideas of the 7 layer OSI model. Where all layers are included and configured to ensure a more secure network. It all has to work in harmony in order to work to send information from one environment to another. With the foundational ideas of the OSI, there’s also smaller, but just as important or critical additions. There’s also many ways that a segmented critical network can fail, because of a poor infrastructure. It only takes a single compromise to make the network a huge security risk.   
	There’s protocols that can better secure segmented networks compared to others. Using TCP is far better to use in such critical networks compared to the UDP protocol. This is because of how TCP works compared to UDP. In the IT/OT environment, using protocols with specific ports that are more secure than others like HTTPS and SSH, to do tasks. Keeping up to date with the more new and secure ports and protocols helps improve overall security in all environments across a network.
